title: Acne Vulgaris
subtitle: The most common skin condition worldwide, affecting up to 85% of people at some point in their lives. Acne occurs when hair follicles become clogged with oil, dead skin cells, and bacteria.

sections.title: Symptoms
sections.intro: Acne affects approximately 650 million people globally. While commonly associated with teenage years, acne can occur at any age and can have significant effects on self-esteem and mental health.
items: Whiteheads, closed clogged pores
Blackheads, open clogged pores darkened by oxidation
Papules, small, tender red bumps
Pustules, pimples with pus at the tip
Nodules, large, solid, painful lumps deep in the skin
Cysts, painful, pus-filled lumps that can cause scarring

sections.title: Causes
sections.intro: Acne develops when four main factors combine: excess oil production, clogged hair follicles, bacteria, and inflammation.
items: Propionibacterium acnes (C. acnes) bacteria overgrowth
Excess sebum production triggered by androgens
Hormonal changes, puberty, menstrual cycle, pregnancy
Certain medications, corticosteroids, lithium
High-glycaemic diet and dairy may worsen acne
Stress increases sebum production indirectly

sections.title: Prevention
items: Wash face twice daily with gentle, non-comedogenic cleanser
Use oil-free, non-comedogenic moisturisers and sunscreen
Do not pick or squeeze pimples, causes scarring
Change pillowcases frequently
Keep hair clean and off face
Reduce high-glycaemic foods and dairy if they trigger breakouts

sections.title: Treatment
items: Topical retinoids (Tretinoin, Adapalene), unclog pores
Benzoyl peroxide, kills acne bacteria
Topical or oral antibiotics for moderate acne
Oral contraceptives for hormonal acne in women
Isotretinoin (Accutane) for severe nodular acne
Chemical peels and laser therapy for scarring

facts: Early treatment prevents permanent acne scars
